project: 혐오체인 · 한국어 유해표현 분석 웹 페이지

runtime.serving: Flask web app (API + page), same input sent to both models

input.preprocessing_at_inference: none beyond the vectorizer (raw text → character n-grams)

models.name: 모델 A · 6종 통합 이진 유해 분류기

training_data.corpus: 6 Korean sources merged (NIKL, UnSmile, KOLD, K-MHaS, K-HATERS, BEEP) → 311,661 rows
training_data.target: source labels mapped to clean=0 / harmful=1; contradictory labels excluded

models.model_selection: 4 settings (3–5/2–5 gram × 60k/200k features) compared on validation Macro-F1
limitations: test is an internal split of the same 6 sources, not an independent external benchmark
character n-grams miss negation/quotation context (e.g. '너는 바보가 아니야.' 43.80 → harmful)
short inputs can be decided by one fragment (e.g. '시래기' 74.33 via '래기')
label definitions differ by source; K-HATERS clean false-positive rate 38.8% on test
models.experimental_not_deployed: hold rule (43 ≤ score < 48, or ≤2 fragments with ≥60% share and score < 80 → review): test review 4.79%, auto-decided clean FPR 27.86% → 23.64%

models.name: 모델 B · K-HATERS 평점 점수 모델 (Hate · 공격성 · 욕설)

training_data.split: official train / validation / test after cleaning (empty text, rating conflicts, cross-split duplicates removed)

targets.hate: max(gender, age, disability, job, race, religion, politics)

training_data.text_normalization: limited normalization of 8 expression patterns (v2), chosen on validation MAE

calibration.selection: validation NLL over 0.5/0.75/1/1.5/2/3 (all three heads chose 1.0)

models.decision: no threshold; three scores are displayed
limitations: scores are expected grade values, not probabilities of being correct or harm severity
weak (grade 1) hate is often predicted as grade 0
separate data and model from model A; K-HATERS text overlaps model A's corpus, so B must not be evaluated on A's test split
